=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status:** Privileged / for negotiation use

---

## 0. Preliminary point: the "Reviewer Efficiency Note"

Before the substance: the Seller's package contains a note stating that clauses marked **[STANDARD]** "have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny" and that the parties "have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package."

**We should disregard this entirely.** Nothing in our instructions or the deal record indicates Wattlebridge has agreed any of these positions. The [STANDARD] tag is the Seller's label, not an agreed status, and virtually every clause carrying it is one of the most buyer-adverse in the package (liability cap, knowledge exclusion, Riverlark release, Ironquay indemnity). We should treat the note as a negotiating tactic, review every clause on its merits, and respond in writing that no clause is agreed until the SPA is signed. We may also want to put on record that we do not accept characterisations of "agreed" positions that have not been agreed.

---

## 1. Material issues – analysis and reasoning

### 1.1 Fundamental and title warranties swept into the general regime (HIGH)

**Seller position:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same 20% cap and 18-month limit "for administrative simplicity"; the limitation, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions in cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply to "all Claims of any nature"; cl 12.3 applies all limitations to all Claims unless expressly carved out.

**Why it matters:** Title and capacity are the foundation of the deal. If Harbourglass does not own the shares or lacks authority to sell, we have lost up to AUD 24m, not AUD 4.8m. Market practice in Australian M&A is that fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, no insolvency) are capped at 100% of price and survive for 6–7 years (or the statutory limitation period). "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to accept a 80% haircut on the core protection of the transaction.

The "all Claims of any nature" drafting also matters because it would, on its face, sweep in: indemnity claims (Ironquay, pre-Completion tax, the DD-006 incident, Riverlark), claims for fraud or wilful concealment, leakage claims under the cash-free/debt-free mechanics, and claims for breach of Seller covenants (e.g., conduct between signing and Completion). Caps and time bars on those categories are not market.

**Recommendation:**
- Fundamental warranties: 100% of price cap; 7-year claims period (or at least 6).
- Tax warranties and tax indemnity: 100% cap (or separate higher cap); claims period = 7 years / until expiry of ATO amendment periods plus a margin.
- Express carve-outs from all caps, thresholds, time limits and exclusive-remedy provisions for: fraud, dishonesty, wilful concealment; specific indemnities; leakage/completion accounts adjustments; Seller covenants; cl 12.3 to be reversed so limitations apply *only* where expressly stated.

### 1.2 General warranty cap, basket and time limit (MEDIUM)

**Seller position:** 20% cap (AUD 4.8m); de minimis AUD 25k; basket AUD 250k, *deductible* (excess only); 18 months.

**Reasoning:** The 20% cap and 18 months are within the range of what sellers open with in a AUD 24m private deal, but each element is at the seller-favourable end:
- A deductible basket means the first AUD 250k of loss is always ours. Buyer practice is a *tipping* basket (once exceeded, recover from dollar one). This is a direct AUD 250k value point.
- AUD 25k de minimis on a business this size is high relative to likely individual claims (e.g., a single payroll-tax underpayment or a supplier dispute). AUD 10–15k is more appropriate.
- 18 months is less than two audit cycles. We should seek 24 months for general warranties so at least one full set of post-Completion accounts and one tax return have been completed.
- The cap should be 30–50% if W&I insurance is not being used; if it is, the structure changes and we should discuss retention and the insurer's position.

**Recommendation:** Tipping basket; de minimis AUD 10–15k; 24 months; cap 30–40% as an opening counter (or recalibrated to the W&I retention).

### 1.3 General disclosure of the data room and public registers (HIGH)

**Seller position:** Everything in the data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records" is disclosed against all warranties (Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2).

**Reasoning:** General disclosure of the entire data room means every warranty is qualified by whatever is buried in any document, regardless of whether the problem was apparent. Combined with the cl 8.3 knowledge exclusion (below) this would hollow out the warranty package almost completely. "Publicly searchable corporate records" is an open-ended category — it could include ASIC, PPSR, court lists, IP Australia, and any regulator's register — that we have not searched comprehensively.

Note also that the Disclosure Letter is dated as at 22 September 2026 and we are now in November. Anything added to the data room after that date is not disclosed, and the Seller will presumably try to bring down disclosure at Completion.

**Recommendation:**
- Disclosure should be limited to matters **fairly disclosed** (i.e., with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter) in the Disclosure Letter and the specific DD documents listed, not the data room generally.
- Public records: limit to specified ASIC and PPSR searches at a specified date, if at all.
- No bring-down disclosure at Completion without a Buyer termination/price-adjustment right for material new disclosure.
- Clause 1.4 (nothing admits that "any consent, payment, notice... is legally required") is a non-admission clause; harmless in itself but it reinforces that the Seller is deliberately not conceding Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay or DD-006 are issues. Our specific indemnities must therefore stand on their own facts, not on any Seller admission.

### 1.4 Clause 8.3 – Buyer knowledge exclusion (HIGH)

**Seller position:** No claim for any matter of which the Buyer *or its advisers* had knowledge, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."

**Reasoning:** This is one of the most damaging clauses in the package:
- "Discoverable" is a constructive knowledge test. It means we lose the claim not because we knew, but because we theoretically could have found it. Combined with general data-room disclosure, the Seller would be able to say almost anything was "discoverable."
- Imputing advisers' knowledge means any fact seen by any junior associate or any accountant on the DD team is deemed known to Wattlebridge.
- The whole purpose of taking warranties on a disclosed matter is that the Seller bears the risk of what the disclosure does not reveal. This clause reverses the allocation.

**Recommendation:** Delete cl 8.3. Fallback: restrict to **actual** knowledge of a named short list of deal-team individuals (not advisers), of facts that would reasonably be understood to constitute a breach, as at signing — and in any event not applicable to fundamental warranties, tax, or the specific indemnities. Alternatively, accept a pro-sandbagging clause stating that Buyer knowledge does not affect warranty claims, with disclosure being the only mechanism for qualification.

### 1.5 Bluefen change-of-control consent (HIGH – deal-critical)

**Facts:** DD-002 shows Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue, ~30% of the Company. Clause 11.2 requires consent on change of control; cl 11.3 imposes conditions. The Disclosure Letter confirms **no final written consent and no evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied**.

**Seller position:** "Reasonable endeavours" and the condition is satisfied "on delivery of the counterparty's written consent."

**Reasoning:** Losing 30% of revenue at Completion would fundamentally change the valuation. The Seller's formulation has two problems:
- "Reasonable endeavours" is the lowest standard; the Seller controls the Bluefen relationship until Completion and should be held to **all reasonable endeavours** or **best endeavours**.
- "Satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent" would let the Seller tender a conditional, qualified or revocable consent — or one that triggers cl 11.3 conditions (e.g., price concessions, guarantees, term changes) that we would have to absorb post-Completion.

**Recommendation:**
- Condition precedent: unconditional, irrevocable written consent from Bluefen in a form approved by the Buyer (acting reasonably), with all cl 11.3 conditions satisfied or waived, and confirmation Bluefen has no outstanding claim/termination right.
- Buyer-only waiver right; long-stop date.
- Fallback if the Seller resists: price adjustment / deferred consideration tied to Bluefen revenue retention for 12–24 months post-Completion, plus a specific indemnity for loss of the contract due to the change of control.
- Request the Seller's correspondence with Bluefen to date and an update now (the letter is six weeks old).

### 1.6 Riverlark facility – release "following Completion" (HIGH – structural)

**Facts:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; change-of-control at cl 8.1; discharge at cl 9.2; not repaid; no discharge of security in the data room.

**Seller position:** Release to be provided *after* Completion.

**Reasoning:** The deal is debt-free/cash-free. A post-Completion release means:
- At Completion, Wattlebridge would own a company that is in default under cl 8.1 (change-of-control) of a AUD 3.2m facility, with security over the assets and possibly over the shares. Riverlark could accelerate against *our* subsidiary.
- The AUD 3.2m must be deducted from the price under the debt-free mechanics. If it is "addressed" post-Completion but not in the funds flow, there is a real risk of double-counting or of the debt simply staying with the Company.
- Any Seller undertaking to procure a release after Completion is only as good as the Seller's covenant and is subject (on their drafting) to the 20% cap and 18-month bar.

**Recommendation:**
- Repayment of Riverlark out of the purchase price **at Completion** via the funds flow, with the payoff letter, deed of release and PPSR discharge (and any mortgage/charge release and any guarantor release) delivered **at Completion** as Completion deliverables.
- Riverlark's consent/waiver of cl 8.1 (or a payoff letter confirming release on repayment) as a condition precedent.
- Confirm whether any Seller or director guarantees exist and ensure they are released with no recourse to the Company.
- Debt definition must expressly capture the facility, accrued interest, break costs and fees.

### 1.7 DD-005 Completion bonuses – AUD 420,000 omitted from funds flow (HIGH – price leakage)

**Facts:** Conditional Completion bonuses of AUD 420k, payable on Completion and continued employment. Not in the funds flow. No disclosure on payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs.

**Seller position:** "A matter for the Seller and not separately itemised."

**Reasoning:** The bonuses are a liability of **the Company**, triggered by Completion. Unless they are paid by the Seller or deducted from the price, Wattlebridge will fund them post-Completion out of the business it has just bought — i.e., a AUD 420k price increase, plus superannuation guarantee (~12%), payroll tax (NSW ~5.45% above threshold) and possibly leave accruals, so a true cost closer to AUD 490–500k. The Seller saying it is "a matter for the Seller" while simultaneously keeping it out of the funds flow is internally inconsistent — if it is for the Seller, it must appear as a Seller-funded line.

**Recommendation:**
- Treat as Transaction Expenses / Debt in the price adjustment: AUD 420k **grossed up** for superannuation, payroll tax and on-costs, deducted from the price or paid by the Seller through payroll at Completion.
- Specific indemnity for any further transaction bonuses, retention or change-of-control payments not disclosed.
- Confirm "continued employment" condition — if any bonus falls due post-Completion (e.g., 6 months after), it must still be a Seller cost.

### 1.8 Ironquay IP – SOW3 Project Materials not owned (HIGH – title to IP)

**Facts:** DD-004 cl 7.3: IP in SOW3 Project Materials transfers only on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180k outstanding. No receipt, no confirmatory assignment.

**Seller position:** Existing indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment, "considered adequate."

**Reasoning:** Paperbark is an analytics company — its value is its IP. On the face of DD-004, Paperbark does **not currently own** the SOW3 deliverables; Ironquay does. An indemnity capped at the AUD 180k payment only covers the fee; it does not cover (a) Ironquay refusing to assign or asserting broader rights, (b) third-party claims, (c) the value of the product if it must be re-developed, or (d) loss of customer revenue if the product incorporating SOW3 code must be withdrawn. The indemnity would also, on the Seller's drafting, be subject to the general cap and 18-month bar.

**Recommendation:**
- Condition precedent / Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees and a **confirmatory deed of assignment** from Ironquay of all IP in the SOW3 Project Materials (with moral rights consents) in Buyer-approved form.
- The AUD 180k to be paid by the Seller (or deducted from price).
- Unlimited-in-amount (or 100%-capped), 6-year specific indemnity for any claim by Ironquay or loss arising from Paperbark not owning or being unable to use the SOW3 materials.
- Expand IP warranties: the Company owns or validly licenses all IP used in the business; no outstanding amounts to contractors conditioning IP transfer; all employee/contractor IP assignments in place. Ask for the full list of SOWs and contractors — if Ironquay's SOW3 has this structure, SOW1 and SOW2 may too.

### 1.9 DD-006 data export / privacy incident (MEDIUM-HIGH)

**Facts:** Download link sent to an unintended external email; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). Unknown whether accessed; investigation preliminary; no determination on notification.

**Seller position:** "Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material."

**Reasoning:** Under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth), an eligible data breach requires assessment within 30 days and notification to the OAIC and affected individuals if likely to result in serious harm. The incident is dated on or before 22 September 2026; it is now 5 November. If the assessment was not completed in 30 days, the Company may already be non-compliant. Penalties under the post-2022 regime are significant (up to the greater of AUD 50m, 3× benefit, or 30% of turnover for serious interferences). Even if the data is business-contact information (which may fall under the employee-records/business-contact gloss), customer contracts (notably Bluefen) will have their own confidentiality and breach-notification obligations, and an analytics company's customers are highly sensitive to this. The Seller's characterisation ("not expected to be material") is an opinion, expressly disclaimed in Disclosure Letter 1.4 and 11.

**Recommendation:**
- Immediate request: the investigation file, the 30-day assessment, confirmation of whether the recipient has confirmed deletion/non-access, and whether any customer (particularly Bluefen) was notified or is contractually entitled to notice.
- Pre-Completion covenant: Seller to complete the assessment and make any required notifications before Completion, in consultation with the Buyer.
- Specific indemnity (outside caps/time limits, minimum 6 years) for all loss arising from the DD-006 incident, including regulatory penalties, notification costs, customer claims and remediation.
- Data protection and cyber warranties given at signing and Completion without general-disclosure qualification for this matter beyond what is in Schedule 6.

### 1.10 Sandbar supplier renewals – AUD 330k (MEDIUM)

**Facts:** Three related renewals of AUD 110k each (DD-008, DD-011), to be "read together for timing/scope." Seller does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.

**Reasoning:** The splitting of a AUD 330k commitment into three AUD 110k pieces, documented across two DD indices, is a pattern that warrants attention — it may be innocent, but it is also how a commitment is kept under materiality thresholds or approval limits. We need to know: are these renewals already committed (so a Company liability at Completion), do they fall due between signing and Completion (so a pre-Completion conduct issue), and are they genuinely necessary to the business? If they are committed and relate to pre-Completion periods, they should be captured as debt-like items or accrued in working capital.

**Recommendation:** Request the three contracts and renewal notices; confirm termination rights; include in the working capital/debt-like item analysis; conduct-of-business covenants should prohibit new commitments above AUD 50k (or an agreed threshold) without Buyer consent, including aggregated related commitments.

### 1.11 Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009) (LOW-MEDIUM)

The Seller frames both as mere notification / assignment provisions not triggered by a share sale. That may be correct, but we should read the clauses ourselves — "assignment" clauses in Australian commercial contracts frequently define a change in control as a deemed assignment. We should require: (a) a warranty that no contract (listed or otherwise) contains a change-of-control or deemed-assignment provision other than those listed in a schedule, and (b) the Seller to give the DD-007 landlord notification before Completion and provide evidence.

### 1.12 Title – share register only (MEDIUM, interacts with 1.1)

The Seller relies solely on the DD-012 share register and expressly notes we have not verified. We should: run current ASIC company and PPSR searches against Paperbark and Harbourglass (share security interests are registrable); check for any options, convertible notes, employee share schemes or shareholder agreements; obtain Harbourglass's constitution/board approval for the sale; and insist on a 100%-capped title warranty (1.1 above). The Seller's own disclosure here makes acceptance of a 20% cap on title indefensible.

### 1.13 Tax and IP "settled under the general regime" (MEDIUM)

The Seller treats tax and IP warranties as capped at 20% and time-barred at 18 months. Tax exposure for pre-Completion periods survives for the ATO amendment period (generally 4 years from assessment, longer for fraud/evasion), so an 18-month bar leaves Wattlebridge exposed for 2.5+ years. Given the Ironquay issue, IP is also not a "general" matter in this deal.

**Recommendation:** Separate tax indemnity for all pre-Completion tax (including payroll tax and superannuation on the DD-005 bonuses), 7-year period, 100% cap. IP warranties to attract the fundamental-warranty cap, or at minimum a higher cap and longer period.

---

## 2. Cross-cutting points

- **Stale disclosure date.** The Disclosure Letter is as at 22 September 2026 — six weeks stale on issues (Bluefen, Riverlark, DD-006) that are live and moving. Require an updated letter and an update on each open matter now, not just at Completion.
- **Funds flow integrity.** The funds flow must reconcile the AUD 24m headline to: less Riverlark (~AUD 3.2m plus break costs), less Ironquay AUD 180k, less DD-005 bonuses grossed up (~AUD 490k+), less any other Debt/Transaction Expenses, plus/minus working capital. On the Seller's current draft, roughly AUD 3.9m of known items are either outside the funds flow or deferred.
- **W&I insurance.** If W&I is contemplated, confirm now — it changes the cap discussion but will not cover known issues (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses), which must still be dealt with by specific indemnities or price mechanics.
- **Conduct between signing and Completion.** Not addressed in the Seller update. Given the Sandbar pattern and the DD-006 incident, we need robust interim covenants and a Buyer consent right.

---

## 3. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Buyer response | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | "Efficiency note" | [STANDARD] = cleared | Reject; nothing agreed; review all clauses | — |
| 1 | Fundamental/title/tax warranties | 20% cap, 18 months | 100% cap, 7 years; carve-outs for fraud, indemnities, covenants, leakage; reverse cl 12.3 | High |
| 2 | General warranty limits | 20% / AUD 25k / AUD 250k deductible / 18m | 30–40% / AUD 10–15k / tipping basket / 24m | Medium |
| 3 | General disclosure | Whole data room + public records | Fair disclosure of specified documents only; no open-ended public records | High |
| 4 | Cl 8.3 knowledge | Constructive knowledge incl. advisers | Delete; fallback actual knowledge of named individuals, excluding fundamentals/indemnities | High |
| 5 | Bluefen consent | Reasonable endeavours; any written consent | CP: unconditional, Buyer-approved consent + cl 11.3 satisfied; fallback deferred consideration/indemnity | High |
| 6 | Riverlark | Release post-Completion | Repay at Completion via funds flow; release/PPSR discharge as Completion deliverable; consent as CP | High |
| 7 | DD-005 bonuses | Omitted from funds flow | Deduct AUD 420k grossed up for super/payroll tax; indemnity for undisclosed payments | High |
| 8 | Ironquay IP | Indemnity capped at SOW3 fee | CP: payment + confirmatory IP assignment; uncapped 6-yr indemnity; broaden IP warranties; review all SOWs | High |
| 9 | DD-006 incident | "Not material" | Full investigation file; complete 30-day assessment/notification pre-Completion; uncapped 6-yr indemnity | Med-High |
| 10 | Sandbar renewals | Ordinary course | Review contracts; debt-like/working capital treatment; interim covenant with aggregation | Medium |
| 11 | Lease / Mossvale | Notification only | Verify deemed-assignment language; schedule of all CoC clauses; evidence of notification | Low-Med |
| 12 | Title | Share register only | ASIC/PPSR searches; check options/SHA; 100% cap | Medium |
| 13 | Tax / IP | General regime | Separate tax indemnity 7 yrs/100%; IP at fundamental level | Medium |

**Immediate next steps:**
1. Reply to Seller's counsel rejecting the "efficiency note" and confirming all clauses remain open.
2. Request an updated Disclosure Letter and status updates on Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay and DD-006 as at today.
3. Issue a revised funds flow capturing Riverlark, Ironquay and the grossed-up bonuses.
4. Circulate our mark-up of cl 8.3, 9.3, 12, 13 and 20.5 with the carve-out structure above, plus specific indemnity schedule.

Please let me know if you would like me to draft the response letter to Seller's counsel or the mark-up of the limitation clauses.

- Express carve-outs from all caps, thresholds, time limits and exclusive-remedy provisions for: fraud, dishonesty, wilful concealment; specific indemnities; leakage/completion accounts adjustments; Seller covenants; cl 12.3 to be reversed so limitations apply *only* where expressly stated.

### 1.2 General warranty cap, basket and time limit (MEDIUM)

**Seller position:** 20% cap (AUD 4.8m); de minimis AUD 25k; basket AUD 250k, *deductible* (excess only); 18 months.

**Reasoning:** The 20% cap and 18 months are within the range of what sellers open with in a AUD 24m private deal, but each element is at the seller-favourable end:
- A deductible basket means the first AUD 250k of loss is always ours. Buyer practice is a *tipping* basket (once exceeded, recover from dollar one). This is a direct AUD 250k value point.
- AUD 25k de minimis on a business this size is high relative to likely individual claims (e.g., a single payroll-tax underpayment or a supplier dispute). AUD 10–15k is more appropriate.
- 18 months is less than two audit cycles. We should seek 24 months for general warranties so at least one full set of post-Completion accounts and one tax return have been completed.
- The cap should be 30–50% if W&I insurance is not being used; if it is, the structure changes and we should discuss retention and the insurer's position.

**Recommendation:** Tipping basket; de minimis AUD 10–15k; 24 months; cap 30–40% as an opening counter (or recalibrated to the W&I retention).

### 1.3 General disclosure of the data room and public registers (HIGH)

**Seller position:** Everything in the data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records" is disclosed against all warranties (Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2).

**Reasoning:** General disclosure of the entire data room means every warranty is qualified by whatever is buried in any document, regardless of whether the problem was apparent. Combined with the cl 8.3 knowledge exclusion (below) this would hollow out the warranty package almost completely. "Publicly searchable corporate records" is an open-ended category — it could include ASIC, PPSR, court lists, IP Australia, and any regulator's register — that we have not searched comprehensively.

Note also that the Disclosure Letter is dated as at 22 September 2026 and we are now in November. Anything added to the data room after that date is not disclosed, and the Seller will presumably try to bring down disclosure at Completion.

**Recommendation:**
- Disclosure should be limited to matters **fairly disclosed** (i.e., with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter) in the Disclosure Letter and the specific DD documents listed, not the data room generally.
- Public records: limit to specified ASIC and PPSR searches at a specified date, if at all.
- No bring-down disclosure at Completion without a Buyer termination/price-adjustment right for material new disclosure.
- Clause 1.4 (nothing admits that "any consent, payment, notice... is legally required") is a non-admission clause; harmless in itself but it reinforces that the Seller is deliberately not conceding Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay or DD-006 are issues. Our specific indemnities must therefore stand on their own facts, not on any Seller admission.

### 1.4 Clause 8.3 – Buyer knowledge exclusion (HIGH)

**Seller position:** No claim for any matter of which the Buyer *or its advisers* had knowledge, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."

**Reasoning:** This is one of the most damaging clauses in the package:
- "Discoverable" is a constructive knowledge test. It means we lose the claim not because we knew, but because we theoretically could have found it. Combined with general data-room disclosure, the Seller would be able to say almost anything was "discoverable."
- Imputing advisers' knowledge means any fact seen by any junior associate or any accountant on the DD team is deemed known to Wattlebridge.
- The whole purpose of taking warranties on a disclosed matter is that the Seller bears the risk of what the disclosure does not reveal. This clause reverses the allocation.

**Recommendation:** Delete cl 8.3. Fallback: restrict to **actual** knowledge of a named short list of deal-team individuals (not advisers), of facts that would reasonably be understood to constitute a breach, as at signing — and in any event not applicable to fundamental warranties, tax, or the specific indemnities. Alternatively, accept a pro-sandbagging clause stating that Buyer knowledge does not affect warranty claims, with disclosure being the only mechanism for qualification.

### 1.5 Bluefen change-of-control consent (HIGH – deal-critical)

**Facts:** DD-002 shows Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue, ~30% of the Company. Clause 11.2 requires consent on change of control; cl 11.3 imposes conditions. The Disclosure Letter confirms **no final written consent and no evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied**.

**Seller position:** "Reasonable endeavours" and the condition is satisfied "on delivery of the counterparty's written consent."

**Reasoning:** Losing 30% of revenue at Completion would fundamentally change the valuation. The Seller's formulation has two problems:
- "Reasonable endeavours" is the lowest standard; the Seller controls the Bluefen relationship until Completion and should be held to **all reasonable endeavours** or **best endeavours**.
- "Satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent" would let the Seller tender a conditional, qualified or revocable consent — or one that triggers cl 11.3 conditions (e.g., price concessions, guarantees, term changes) that we would have to absorb post-Completion.

**Recommendation:**
- Condition precedent: unconditional, irrevocable written consent from Bluefen in a form approved by the Buyer (acting reasonably), with all cl 11.3 conditions satisfied or waived, and confirmation Bluefen has no outstanding claim/termination right.
- Buyer-only waiver right; long-stop date.
- Fallback if the Seller resists: price adjustment / deferred consideration tied to Bluefen revenue retention for 12–24 months post-Completion, plus a specific indemnity for loss of the contract due to the change of control.
- Request the Seller's correspondence with Bluefen to date and an update now (the letter is six weeks old).

### 1.6 Riverlark facility – release "following Completion" (HIGH – structural)

**Facts:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; change-of-control at cl 8.1; discharge at cl 9.2; not repaid; no discharge of security in the data room.

**Seller position:** Release to be provided *after* Completion.

**Reasoning:** The deal is debt-free/cash-free. A post-Completion release means:
- At Completion, Wattlebridge would own a company that is in default under cl 8.1 (change-of-control) of a AUD 3.2m facility, with security over the assets and possibly over the shares. Riverlark could accelerate against *our* subsidiary.
- The AUD 3.2m must be deducted from the price under the debt-free mechanics. If it is "addressed" post-Completion but not in the funds flow, there is a real risk of double-counting or of the debt simply staying with the Company.
- Any Seller undertaking to procure a release after Completion is only as good as the Seller's covenant and is subject (on their drafting) to the 20% cap and 18-month bar.

**Recommendation:**
- Repayment of Riverlark out of the purchase price **at Completion** via the funds flow, with the payoff letter, deed of release and PPSR discharge (and any mortgage/charge release and any guarantor release) delivered **at Completion** as Completion deliverables.
- Riverlark's consent/waiver of cl 8.1 (or a payoff letter confirming release on repayment) as a condition precedent.
- Confirm whether any Seller or director guarantees exist and ensure they are released with no recourse to the Company.
- Debt definition must expressly capture the facility, accrued interest, break costs and fees.

### 1.7 DD-005 Completion bonuses – AUD 420,000 omitted from funds flow (HIGH – price leakage)

**Facts:** Conditional Completion bonuses of AUD 420k, payable on Completion and continued employment. Not in the funds flow. No disclosure on payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs.

**Seller position:** "A matter for the Seller and not separately itemised."

**Reasoning:** The bonuses are a liability of **the Company**, triggered by Completion. Unless they are paid by the Seller or deducted from the price, Wattlebridge will fund them post-Completion out of the business it has just bought — i.e., a AUD 420k price increase, plus superannuation guarantee (~12%), payroll tax (NSW ~5.45% above threshold) and possibly leave accruals, so a true cost closer to AUD 490–500k. The Seller saying it is "a matter for the Seller" while simultaneously keeping it out of the funds flow is internally inconsistent — if it is for the Seller, it must appear as a Seller-funded line.

**Recommendation:**
- Treat as Transaction Expenses / Debt in the price adjustment: AUD 420k **grossed up** for superannuation, payroll tax and on-costs, deducted from the price or paid by the Seller through payroll at Completion.
- Specific indemnity for any further transaction bonuses, retention or change-of-control payments not disclosed.
- Confirm "continued employment" condition — if any bonus falls due post-Completion (e.g., 6 months after), it must still be a Seller cost.

### 1.8 Ironquay IP – SOW3 Project Materials not owned (HIGH – title to IP)

**Facts:** DD-004 cl 7.3: IP in SOW3 Project Materials transfers only on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180k outstanding. No receipt, no confirmatory assignment.

**Seller position:** Existing indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment, "considered adequate."

**Reasoning:** Paperbark is an analytics company — its value is its IP. On the face of DD-004, Paperbark does **not currently own** the SOW3 deliverables; Ironquay does. An indemnity capped at the AUD 180k payment only covers the fee; it does not cover (a) Ironquay refusing to assign or asserting broader rights, (b) third-party claims, (c) the value of the product if it must be re-developed, or (d) loss of customer revenue if the product incorporating SOW3 code must be withdrawn. The indemnity would also, on the Seller's drafting, be subject to the general cap and 18-month bar.

**Recommendation:**
- Condition precedent / Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees and a **confirmatory deed of assignment** from Ironquay of all IP in the SOW3 Project Materials (with moral rights consents) in Buyer-approved form.
- The AUD 180k to be paid by the Seller (or deducted from price).
- Unlimited-in-amount (or 100%-capped), 6-year specific indemnity for any claim by Ironquay or loss arising from Paperbark not owning or being unable to use the SOW3 materials.
- Expand IP warranties: the Company owns or validly licenses all IP used in the business; no outstanding amounts to contractors conditioning IP transfer; all employee/contractor IP assignments in place. Ask for the full list of SOWs and contractors — if Ironquay's SOW3 has this structure, SOW1 and SOW2 may too.

### 1.9 DD-006 data export / privacy incident (MEDIUM-HIGH)

**Facts:** Download link sent to an unintended external email; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). Unknown whether accessed; investigation preliminary; no determination on notification.

**Seller position:** "Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material."

**Reasoning:** Under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth), an eligible data breach requires assessment within 30 days and notification to the OAIC and affected individuals if likely to result in serious harm. The incident is dated on or before 22 September 2026; it is now 5 November. If the assessment was not completed in 30 days, the Company may already be non-compliant. Penalties under the post-2022 regime are significant (up to the greater of AUD 50m, 3× benefit, or 30% of turnover for serious interferences). Even if the data is business-contact information (which may fall under the employee-records/business-contact gloss), customer contracts (notably Bluefen) will have their own confidentiality and breach-notification obligations, and an analytics company's customers are highly sensitive to this. The Seller's characterisation ("not expected to be material") is an opinion, expressly disclaimed in Disclosure Letter 1.4 and 11.

**Recommendation:**
- Immediate request: the investigation file, the 30-day assessment, confirmation of whether the recipient has confirmed deletion/non-access, and whether any customer (particularly Bluefen) was notified or is contractually entitled to notice.
- Pre-Completion covenant: Seller to complete the assessment and make any required notifications before Completion, in consultation with the Buyer.
- Specific indemnity (outside caps/time limits, minimum 6 years) for all loss arising from the DD-006 incident, including regulatory penalties, notification costs, customer claims and remediation.
- Data protection and cyber warranties given at signing and Completion without general-disclosure qualification for this matter beyond what is in Schedule 6.

### 1.10 Sandbar supplier renewals – AUD 330k (MEDIUM)

**Facts:** Three related renewals of AUD 110k each (DD-008, DD-011), to be "read together for timing/scope." Seller does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.

**Reasoning:** The splitting of a AUD 330k commitment into three AUD 110k pieces, documented across two DD indices, is a pattern that warrants attention — it may be innocent, but it is also how a commitment is kept under materiality thresholds or approval limits. We need to know: are these renewals already committed (so a Company liability at Completion), do they fall due between signing and Completion (so a pre-Completion conduct issue), and are they genuinely necessary to the business? If they are committed and relate to pre-Completion periods, they should be captured as debt-like items or accrued in working capital.

**Recommendation:** Request the three contracts and renewal notices; confirm termination rights; include in the working capital/debt-like item analysis; conduct-of-business covenants should prohibit new commitments above AUD 50k (or an agreed threshold) without Buyer consent, including aggregated related commitments.

### 1.11 Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009) (LOW-MEDIUM)

The Seller frames both as mere notification / assignment provisions not triggered by a share sale. That may be correct, but we should read the clauses ourselves — "assignment" clauses in Australian commercial contracts frequently define a change in control as a deemed assignment. We should require: (a) a warranty that no contract (listed or otherwise) contains a change-of-control or deemed-assignment provision other than those listed in a schedule, and (b) the Seller to give the DD-007 landlord notification before Completion and provide evidence.

### 1.12 Title – share register only (MEDIUM, interacts with 1.1)

The Seller relies solely on the DD-012 share register and expressly notes we have not verified. We should: run current ASIC company and PPSR searches against Paperbark and Harbourglass (share security interests are registrable); check for any options, convertible notes, employee share schemes or shareholder agreements; obtain Harbourglass's constitution/board approval for the sale; and insist on a 100%-capped title warranty (1.1 above). The Seller's own disclosure here makes acceptance of a 20% cap on title indefensible.

### 1.13 Tax and IP "settled under the general regime" (MEDIUM)

The Seller treats tax and IP warranties as capped at 20% and time-barred at 18 months. Tax exposure for pre-Completion periods survives for the ATO amendment period (generally 4 years from assessment, longer for fraud/evasion), so an 18-month bar leaves Wattlebridge exposed for 2.5+ years. Given the Ironquay issue, IP is also not a "general" matter in this deal.

**Recommendation:** Separate tax indemnity for all pre-Completion tax (including payroll tax and superannuation on the DD-005 bonuses), 7-year period, 100% cap. IP warranties to attract the fundamental-warranty cap, or at minimum a higher cap and longer period.
